options: Securing and maintaining the safety and integrity of data after it has been processed, for future reference
Cleaning and standardising data before it is loaded into a warehouse
Encrypting data while it is in transit between systems
Deleting data as soon as it is no longer needed for daily operations
Collecting personal data minimally and using it ethically
questions.explanation: Data Preservation is about securing and maintaining the safety and integrity of data after it has been processed, for future reference.

questions.stem: Which statement describes data that has been preserved?
options: It can be freely edited but never copied
It cannot be changed and is hardly ever purged or deleted
It must be deleted after seven years in every industry
It is kept only in memory for fast access
It is refreshed daily from the source system
questions.explanation: Data which is preserved cannot be changed and is hardly purged or deleted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three things to consider for Data Preservation?
options: What data is to be preserved
What the retention period is
Which visualisation tool will present the preserved data
Who will be responsible for preserving the data
For how long the data should be kept
questions.explanation: The considerations are what data to preserve, the retention period (how long to keep data) and who is responsible (a custodian). The choice of visualisation tool is not among them.

questions.stem: Who is required for a data repository under Data Preservation?
options: An external auditor
A regulatory body
A data scientist
A custodian
An investor
questions.explanation: A custodian is required for the data repository; someone must be responsible for preserving the data.

questions.stem: Why is it not possible to preserve everything in the current era of big data?
options: Because regulators forbid preserving unstructured data
Because preserved data must be stored on paper
Because only relational databases can preserve data
Because custodians are not allowed to keep data for more than a year
Because big data brings huge semi-structured and unstructured datasets, so one must decide what to preserve and for how long
questions.explanation: With big data's huge semi-structured and unstructured datasets, it is not worth, and not possible, to preserve everything. One must decide what to preserve and for how long.

questions.stem: In the traditional banking example of Data Preservation, for how long is the history of customers who have closed their accounts preserved?
options: Seven years from the day they closed their accounts
One year from the day they opened their accounts
Indefinitely, with no retention limit
Thirty days after the final transaction
Until the next external audit
questions.explanation: Traditionally in the banking sector, the history of customers who have closed their accounts is preserved for seven years from the day they closed them.

questions.stem: Where is a good starting point for deciding which datasets to preserve?
options: The list of the most frequently queried tables
The list of compliance requirements
The list of the largest datasets by storage size
The list of dashboards used by management
The list of datasets with the poorest quality
questions.explanation: One can start from the list of compliance requirements, such as the banking rule of preserving closed-account history for seven years.

questions.stem: In the research field example, which data is preserved when hundreds of tests run daily?
options: Every piece of test data, without exception
Only the data produced on the first day of each month
Only the data which can convince investors to keep investing, until new investment is in
Only the data that failed quality checks
Only the data older than seven years
questions.explanation: In research, where hundreds of tests run daily, not every piece of data is preserved; only the data which can convince investors to keep investing is preserved, until the new investment is in.

questions.stem: Which datastores are given as examples in which certain datasets are chosen for preservation?
options: Spreadsheets, email archives and shared drives
Key-value stores, caches and message queues
Source transactional systems only
Data Warehouse, Data Mart and Data Lake
Backup tapes and printed reports
questions.explanation: In datastores such as a Data Warehouse, a Data Mart or a Data Lake, there are certain datasets to preserve.

questions.stem: Alongside Data Security, Data Privacy, Data Integrity and Data Compliance, to what does Data Preservation refer?
options: The monetisation of the data
The visualisation of the data
The modelling of the data
The transformation of the data
The protection of the data
questions.explanation: Data Preservation, Data Security, Data Privacy, Data Integrity and Data Compliance all refer to the protection of the data.
